subject: physics
question_text: Two bodies are projected with the same speed at angles θ and (90° − θ) with the horizontal. Compare their horizontal ranges.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two ranges
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write both ranges from the same formula before comparing them.
steps.why: Doubling (90° − θ) gives (180° − 2θ), so the second range is the same formula at a supplementary angle.
common_mistakes: Writing the second angle inside the sine as (90° − 2θ) instead of (180° − 2θ).

recall.must_convey: That the second range uses sin of 180 degrees minus 2 theta.

steps.memory_tip: Double the angle first: 2(90° − θ) is 180° − 2θ. With θ = 30° that is 120°, not 30°.

steps.label: The comparison

lines.text: R₁ = R₂ — the two ranges are equal

lines: Example: 30° and 60° land at the same spot,
though the 60° body flies higher and longer.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. State R₁ = R₂ in words. One worked pair of angles secures it.
steps.why: Equal ranges do not mean equal flights: the steeper throw trades forward speed for time in the air, and the two effects cancel exactly.
common_mistakes: Concluding the two paths are identical — the heights and the times of flight differ.

recall.must_convey: That sin of 180 minus 2 theta equals sin 2 theta, so the two ranges are equal.
accept: sin 180 minus 2 theta equals sin 2 theta
reject: sin 180 minus 2 theta is the second range

steps.memory_tip: sin 120° = sin 60° = 0.866. Supplementary angles share a sine, and that closes the proof.

insider_note: Two marks: both ranges written out, then the single line sin(180° − 2θ) = sin 2θ. That identity is the second mark.
